title: Judging with Many Minds: Do More Perspectives Mean Less Prejudice? On Bias Amplifications and Resistance in Multi-Agent Based LLM-as-Judge

paper.authors: Chiyu Ma, Enpei Zhang, Yilun Zhao, Wenjun Liu, Yaning Jia, Peijun Qing, Lin Shi, Arman Cohan, Yujun Yan, Soroush Vosoughi (Dartmouth / Yale)

paper.other_artifacts: Data ships in-repo: data/mtbench_pairwise_data_all.json (4,800 pairs), data/mtbench_pairwise_data_normal_random_sampled.json (480, the experimental set), data/calm_pairwise_data_all.json (439), plus verbose-perturbed variants. analysis/ holds per-model per-bias aggregated JSONs for every cell of Tables 1-4.

dependence.note: LLM judges and critics are the object of study; the consistency rate is computed entirely from model outputs. But every arm is either open-weight (R1-Distilled-Qwen-32B, Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct-Turbo via Together.ai, Qwen1.5-32B-Chat+PINE), a non-OpenAI API (DeepSeek-V3), or gpt-4o-mini - none of which is on the retirement list.

claim.statement: Introducing multi-agent debate amplifies judge bias immediately: for the GPT-4o-mini self-play judge-critic pair the consistency rate falls from round 0 to round 1 on every bias - MT-Bench positivity 0.793 -> 0.667, verbosity 0.716 -> 0.637, bandwagon 0.746 -> 0.667, CoT 0.835 -> 0.731; CALM-Alignment 0.793 -> 0.663, 0.789 -> 0.704, 0.740 -> 0.663, 0.869 -> 0.763 - and does not recover over rounds 2-3 (Table 1).
claim.metric: Consistency rate CR = (1/N) * sum_i I(y_i == y_i_modified): the fraction of pairwise judgements unchanged after a bias-eliciting prompt modification (position swap, verbosity inflation, bandwagon cue, or a CoT-style cue). Higher is better resistance. N = 480 (MT-Bench) or 439 (CALM-Alignment).
claim.claim_type_note: The reported values are consistency, not accuracy; no human gold label is involved in this metric.

gpt4o_mini_judge_gpt4o_mini_critic.index_meaning: [round 0 (single judge, no debate), round 1, round 2, round 3]

claim.original_source: Paper Table 1 (Consistency scores across three rounds of multi-agent debate, MT-Bench and CALM-Alignment); Table 3 for the PINE bias-free critic; Table 14 for the RewardBench replication. All values to three decimals.

budget.assumptions: HYPOTHETICAL and off-study, since gpt-4o-mini is not retiring. Table 1 GPT-4o-mini self-play row only: 919 items x 4 bias types x 2 conditions (original and modified) x (1 round-0 judgement + 3 debate rounds x 2 agent turns) ~= 22,000 calls; ~800 input tokens (question plus two candidate solutions plus debate memory, growing with rounds) and ~150 output tokens against the 512 cap. Round 0 alone would be about 7,400 calls and USD 1.5. Single run at temperature 0.01, matching the paper (no 3-seed multiplier applied).

judgment.rule: ANALYSIS_PLAN section 1 (only if the user decides to run an off-study arm). Primary numbers: the eight round-0 -> round-1 consistency drops for the GPT-4o-mini self-play pair. Survival = each re-run round-0 value inside the bootstrap 95% CI over items of the original (n = 480 or 439, about +/- 3.7 pp) AND the behavioural direction holds: every bias type still drops significantly from round 0 to round 1 and does not recover by round 3. Partial = levels shift but the round-0 > round-1 direction holds for at least three of the four bias types. Death = debate no longer reduces consistency, i.e. the paper's central phenomenon disappears.
judgment.notes: Consistency is a self-comparison (original vs perturbed judgement), so it is robust to absolute-quality drift but sensitive to format compliance: a model that starts refusing or hedging on the NSFW CALM items would corrupt the denominator. The paper's own claim is about the round-0 -> round-1 step, not about the absolute level.

domain_notes: The paper studies whether multi-agent judging (debate and meta-judge) reduces or amplifies four known LLM-judge biases: position (positivity), verbosity, bandwagon and a CoT-style cue. Headline findings: debate sharply amplifies bias after one round and does not recover; meta-judging is more resistant; a bias-free PINE agent (Qwen1.5-32B-Chat with position-bias elimination) helps as a debate critic but much less as a pool member. Everything needed to reproduce it is public under Apache-2.0 - this card is blocked purely because no arm is a retiring snapshot, which makes it a clean negative data point for the census (an alias match on 'gpt-4-turbo' coming from dataset provenance rather than from any API call).
